### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**1** anchor(s) derived from **2** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them. ⚠️ **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/stored-migration.ts`, `packages/spec/src/conversions/stored.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/stored-migration.ts`, `packages/spec/src/conversions/stored.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **169** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ab085a048241b0bf1fde06696fc6cbf659a6707f` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `11c7d86228e8bba20f3b9ccbe40e1282df0bd6a4` — the merge of head `cbdd0231ac500647fbb014dda9f2c0aee3d4c746` into base `ab085a048241b0bf1fde06696fc6cbf659a6707f`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 11c7d86228e8bba20f3b9ccbe40e1282df0bd6a4 && git checkout 11c7d86228e8bba20f3b9ccbe40e1282df0bd6a4
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin ab085a048241b0bf1fde06696fc6cbf659a6707f cbdd0231ac500647fbb014dda9f2c0aee3d4c746 && git checkout -B drift-repro ab085a048241b0bf1fde06696fc6cbf659a6707f && git merge --no-ff cbdd0231ac500647fbb014dda9f2c0aee3d4c746

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ab085a048241b0bf1fde06696fc6cbf659a6707f
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

### ① Derived judgments

- AGENTS.md Prime Directive #12 (lines 253-255). Every new sentence is true on main. "rehydration replays the chain the installed release carries, retired entries included": `applyConversionsToStoredItem` (packages/spec/src/conversions/stored.ts) calls `applyConversions` with `includeRetired: true` pinned, and `apply.ts` line 157 skips a `retiredFromLoadPath` entry only when that flag is off, so every entry the installed registry carries replays and nothing more. "a kit ages out one major after it retires": ADR-0087 D2 window bullet as amended 2026-10-26 and the 2026-10-26 addendum ("lives through the protocol major after the one it retired in, and is removed when the next major is cut"), ruling 6434038284 part 1. The registry census on main confirms the consequence: 111 `retiredAfter` entries, lowest `17.0.0`, no entry at or below 16.x. "run `os migrate meta --stored --apply` on a release that still converts the row, before leaving it": the ADR 2026-07-31 addendum as amended, the changeset's Stored rows bullet (18.2 or earlier, before 18.3) and skills/objectstack-upgrade/SKILL.md § Stored rows all say the same; the flag spelling matches packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/meta.ts. Correct.
- AGENTS.md shape. File length 1050 lines on both trees; the directive still spans lines 245-255 and #13 still starts at 256; the three new lines are 116, 112 and 115 characters. The rule intent is kept: no lenient alias or `??` fallback in a consumer, an alias tolerated only as an ADR-0087 conversion-layer entry (no executor shims) that is declared, loud, tested and removable on a schedule, Strengthens #5. The citation form ("ADR-0087 as amended, ruling 6434038284") is the provenance form the file's own preamble allows (an ADR or ruling record, never an issue number). What the hunk drops: the consequence clause (the PR body names and justifies it: no longer unconditionally true) and the primitive's name `applyConversionsToStoredItem`, which the PR body does not mention; the ADR addendum and both headers still name it, so nothing becomes unfindable. Correct, with one should-fix below.
- packages/spec/src/conversions/stored.ts header, first policy bullet. True against the function below it and against ADR-0087's 2026-07-31 addendum as amended: the bullet now says the chain the installed release carries replays, retired entries included, a kit ages out one major after it retires and its conversion leaves with it, and a row still in that shape must be canonicalized by the stored pass on a release that still carries its conversions. The function docblock lower in the same file (lines 91 and 100 on the head) still says "the **full** ADR-0087 conversion chain (retired entries included)" and "the same full-chain policy"; that names what replays, not for how long, so it stays true and is outside the claimed surface (header only). Correct.
- packages/metadata-protocol/src/stored-migration.ts header, first paragraph. True against `migrateStoredMetadata` (protocol.ts): the pass replays the same chain through `applyConversionsToStoredItem`, and a row no conversion recognises produces no notice, so the `record` closure counts it `canonical` and never itemises it. One loose phrase: "past that, no seam recognizes the row". The seams still read and serve the row; it is the row's shape that no conversion recognises, and the stored pass then counts the row `canonical` (the false-clean SKILL.md § 3.6 warns about). Should-fix wording, not a false statement of policy.
- packages/metadata-protocol/src/stored-migration.ts header, the narrowed "Not load-bearing" paragraph. Inside the claimed surface: it is the same block comment, lines 26-32. True: within the window the release still carries a row's conversions the read path remains the guarantee and nothing gates on the pass having run (no `sys_migration` flag is written; SKILL.md § 3.6 says nothing gates on it); for a row whose conversions the next release drops the pass is the required step, which is the ADR's own amended sentence ("for those rows it is the required one, not an optional one"). Correct, and without it the header would have contradicted its own first paragraph.
- No code or behaviour change: all three hunks lie inside a block comment or Markdown prose; no token outside a comment moved. Confirmed on the diff.

### ② Semver level

- `Clause-②: no`. Correct. The packages/spec/src/** path hint is answered by content: stored.ts is a comment-only hunk in a `.ts` file that is not in `@objectstack/spec` `files[]` (`src/**/*.zod.ts` only); no export, type or accepted shape moves. `Metadata-protocol: none`. Correct: nothing an author can write changes.
- No changeset, `skip-changeset` label. Correct under the repo's rules: AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist step 3 reserves the label for a diff that publishes nothing from any released package, and review-checklist.md routes tests- or docs-only changes to the label, never to an empty changeset. Both packages are published (`private` unset), but a comment-only diff ships no behaviour, API or CHANGELOG-worthy change; `Check Changeset` is `success` on this head. Whether the header comment reaches the built `.d.ts` bytes was not measured (no dist in this checkout, nothing built) and does not move the level.
- Tier: Tier H. `check-governed-merges.mjs --pr 29011` reads 1 of 3 paths on the register (AGENTS.md), landing tier H, 40 changed lines under the size line. The PR lands only on an authorized APPROVED review by an account in `GOVERNED_APPROVERS` and then the owning seat; this record is the contract-tier review owed for the governed rules face and the schema face, not a substitute for that approval. The PR is draft, no auto-merge armed, nothing to disarm.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev `open_questions`: none. Nothing to answer.
- Dev out-of-scope finding (carrier none): spot-checked and confirmed. packages/metadata-core/src/artifact-forward-conversion.ts (lines 23-24, 49, 96), packages/core/src/fallbacks/authored-translation-sync.ts (46-47) and packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts (7024, 22362, 22374) say the full chain replays, retired entries included; that names what replays and none says forever, so they stay true. protocol.ts line 22338's "stays `pending` in `os migrate meta --stored` forever" is about a row never canonicalized, not the claim this card corrects.
- One further text of the same class, outside the card's three and outside the dev's list: packages/spec/src/conversions/apply.ts lines 54-55, "The fixture CI sets it as well, so graduated transforms stay covered forever (ADR-0087 D3)". The 50 aged-out conversions left with their fixtures under #25767, so "forever" is drift there too. Not this PR's surface; a follow-up card for the seat, no carrier on this PR.
- The five gates the dev did not measure are carried by CI on this head: `check:dts-closure` in lint.yml `typecheck-debt` (Type Check · debt ledger) and `typecheck-consumers` (Type Check · consumer gates) and in ci.yml Build Core; `check:dual-build-cjs-loads`, `check:sourcemap-no-sources-content` and `check:lean-entry-closure` in ci.yml Build Core (steps at lines 3036, 3045, 3060, after `pnpm build`); `@objectstack/lint check:doc-formula-expressions` in lint.yml `typecheck-consumers` (line 6307). All three jobs have check-runs on this head (state at record time below).
- The prose gates the rewrite could trip run in lint.yml `lint-repo-tooling` (Lint · repo & tooling gates: `check:pm-skill-id-lint`, `check:pm-governed-prose`, `check:doc-authoring`) and `lint-ci-engine` (Lint · CI, release & engine gates: `check:issue-citations`); the dev reports them green locally on this head, and CI's verdict is read below.
- Author: `objectstack-fleet[bot]` through the relay; no off-relay author to name. Dispatch form: `mode:thread`, Implemented-by is the thread's branch.

### ④ Design judgment

- AGENTS.md: the directive now states the policy the code enforces. Pinned `includeRetired: true` replays every entry the registry carries; the registry on main carries no entry retired at or below 16.x; so "the chain the installed release carries" is the exact invariant, and the old "full chain, retired entries included, forever" would lead an agent to call a 16-era row safe on 18.3. The acceptance scenario holds: an agent reasoning from #12 now tells a user to run the stored pass on a release that still converts the row before moving. The rule loses no prohibition and gains the one action the amended ADR requires. Holds.
- stored.ts: the header's first bullet is the policy the function immediately below implements and matches the ADR's amended 2026-07-31 addendum sentence for sentence. Holds.
- stored-migration.ts: the first paragraph and the narrowed "Not load-bearing" paragraph are now consistent with each other and with `migrateStoredMetadata`; the one loose phrase (should-fix 1) does not misstate the rule. Holds.
- Must-fixes: none.
- Should-fixes: (1) stored-migration.ts header: replace "past that, no seam recognizes the row" with the precise statement, that no conversion recognises the shape, the seam serves the legacy bytes, and this pass then counts the row `canonical`, which is the false-clean an operator must not trust. (2) AGENTS.md: either keep `applyConversionsToStoredItem` by name in the directive or name its removal in the PR body beside the consequence clause. (3) Follow-up card, not this PR: apply.ts lines 54-55 "stay covered forever".
